statement: He returned to Madinah and fell ill about three months later, early in year 11.
alternatives: The illness is dated to the last days of Safar or the first of Rabi' al-Awwal; its length is given as about thirteen days.

statement: Aishah said 'Oh, my head' and he replied 'Rather I should say: Oh, my head'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. The fuller exchange is abridged.

statement: He appointed Usamah ibn Zayd to command an expedition; people criticised it; he said they had criticised his father's command before, that Zayd was worthy and among the dearest to him, and Usamah among the dearest after him.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. That it was bound for the Roman frontier is from the Seerah.

statement: Aishah: when his illness worsened he asked his wives' permission to be nursed in her house; he came out between two men with his feet dragging.
He told Aishah he still felt the pain of the food he ate at Khaybar.

Abu Sa'id: he said a servant was given the choice between this world and what is with Allah and chose the latter; Abu Bakr wept, understanding; he said Abu Bakr was the most generous to him, that he would have taken him as khalil, and that all doors to the mosque be closed except Abu Bakr's.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first half; the rest from memory of the same narration.

statement: He ordered that Abu Bakr lead the prayer; Aishah said he was tender-hearted and would not be heard for weeping; he repeated the order; Abu Bakr led the prayers during the illness.
He counselled regarding the Ansar: accept from their good-doers and overlook their wrongdoers.
Aishah: in his final illness he condemned those who took their prophets' graves as places of worship; otherwise his grave would have been made prominent.
notes: Machine-checked. The narration names the peoples; the script says 'earlier peoples'.

statement: Aishah: Fatimah came walking as he walked; he seated her, whispered to her and she wept, whispered again and she laughed; after his death she said he told her his time had come, that she would be the first of his family to join him, and that she would be the foremost of the women of Paradise.
notes: Direct speech. Content machine-checked in the Muslim dataset (no. 6313) for the first part; the rest from memory. Numbers from memory.

statement: Anas: on Monday, while Abu Bakr led the prayer, he lifted the curtain, stood looking at them, his face like a page of the mushaf, and smiled; they were nearly distracted with joy; Abu Bakr stepped back; he signalled them to complete the prayer and let the curtain fall; he died that day.
